words.en: Provision, what is apportioned of food and of benefit. Lane: razaqa, he provided; rizq is a portion of provision. Penrice: Provision, food. Related: razzaq (provider, a name of Allah), marzuq. Rizq in the lexicon is wider than a salary: anything by which a body or a soul is sustained.
words.fr: Provision, ce qui est departi de nourriture et de benefice. Lane: razaqa, il a pourvu; rizq, une part de provision. Penrice: provision, nourriture. Lie: razzaq, marzuq. Le rizq est plus large qu un salaire: tout ce par quoi un corps ou une ame est soutenu.
words.src: Penrice, A Dictionary and Glossary of the Kor-an, London 1873, s.v. ر ز ق. Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon, London 1863-1893, same root. French sense: Kazimirski, Dictionnaire arabe-francais, Paris 1860, same root. Language fact from those lexicons, not a ruling.

words.en: A wage, a reward. Lane: ajr, hire, reward; ajara, he rewarded, he hired. Penrice: Reward, hire. Related: ajir (a hired worker), istijar (to hire), ujrah. With Allah it is the reward of deeds; with people it is a wage. The lexicon is payment for work.
words.fr: Un salaire, une recompense. Lane: ajr, loyer, recompense; ajara, il a recompense, il a loue. Penrice: recompense, loyer. Lie: ajir, ujrah. Aupres d Allah, recompense des actes; aupres des gens, un salaire. Le lexique est un paiement pour un travail.
words.src: Penrice, A Dictionary and Glossary of the Kor-an, London 1873, s.v. ا ج ر. Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon, London 1863-1893, same root. French sense: Kazimirski, Dictionnaire arabe-francais, Paris 1860, same root. Language fact from those lexicons, not a ruling.

words.en: A sin, a fault; lexically also a tail (the consequence that follows). Lane: dhanb, a sin, a crime; also a tail. Penrice: A sin. Plural dhunub. Related: mudhnib (a sinner). Some lexica note the tail-sense: a sin as what follows the person. Istighfar is sought for dhunub.
words.fr: Un peche, une faute; lexicalement aussi une queue (la suite qui suit). Lane: dhanb, peche, crime; aussi une queue. Penrice: un peche. Pluriel dhunub. Lie: mudhnib. Certains lexiques notent le sens de queue: un peche comme ce qui suit la personne.
words.src: Penrice, A Dictionary and Glossary of the Kor-an, London 1873, s.v. ذ ن ب. Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon, London 1863-1893, same root. French sense: Kazimirski, Dictionnaire arabe-francais, Paris 1860, same root. Language fact from those lexicons, not a ruling.

words.en: Forgiveness as a covering of the sin. Lane: maghfirah, pardon. See istighfar. Penrice: Forgiveness. It is Allah's covering, not the slave's claim. Related: ghaffar, ghafur, ghufran, istighfar.
words.fr: Pardon comme couverture du peche. Lane: maghfirah, pardon. Voir istighfar. Penrice: pardon. C est la couverture d Allah, non la pretention du serviteur. Lie: ghaffar, ghafur, ghufran, istighfar.
words.src: Penrice, A Dictionary and Glossary of the Kor-an, London 1873, s.v. غ ف ر. Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon, London 1863-1893, same root. French sense: Kazimirski, Dictionnaire arabe-francais, Paris 1860, same root. Language fact from those lexicons, not a ruling.

words.en: Mercy, compassion, a tender benefit. Lane: rahmah, mercy. Penrice: Mercy. Related: Rahman, Rahim, rahim (womb), tarahum. A rain can be called rahmah as a mercy sent down. The womb (rahim) is named from this tenderness.
words.fr: Misericorde, compassion, un bien tendre. Lane: rahmah, misericorde. Penrice: misericorde. Lie: Rahman, Rahim, rahim (matrice), tarahum. Une pluie peut etre dite rahmah. La matrice est nommee de cette tendresse.
words.src: Penrice, A Dictionary and Glossary of the Kor-an, London 1873, s.v. ر ح م. Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon, London 1863-1893, same root. French sense: Kazimirski, Dictionnaire arabe-francais, Paris 1860, same root. Language fact from those lexicons, not a ruling.

words.en: Humility that appears in the limbs from a lowered heart. Lane: khasha'a, he was lowly, he cast down his eyes; khushu' is humility. Penrice: To be humble. Related: khashi'. Quran 23:2: those who are humble in their salah. The lexicon is a lowering, not a theatre of tears.
words.fr: Humilite qui parait dans les membres d un coeur abaisse. Lane: khasha a, il a ete humble, il a baisse les yeux; khushu, humilite. Penrice: etre humble. Lie: khashi. Coran 23:2. Le lexique est un abaissement, non un theatre de larmes.
words.src: Penrice, A Dictionary and Glossary of the Kor-an, London 1873, s.v. خ ش ع. Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon, London 1863-1893, same root. French sense: Kazimirski, Dictionnaire arabe-francais, Paris 1860, same root. Language fact from those lexicons, not a ruling.

words.en: Fear mixed with knowledge and awe. Lane: khashiya, he feared; khashyah is fear. Penrice: To fear. The Quran says of the scholars that they fear Allah: khashyah in that speech is not panic, it is fear that comes with ilm. Related: khashi (one who fears). Distinct from khawf in shade: khashyah is often fear of a great one you know.
words.fr: Crainte melee de savoir et d awe. Lane: khashiya, il a craint; khashyah, crainte. Penrice: craindre. Le Coran dit des savants qu ils craignent Allah: khashyah n est pas la panique, c est la crainte avec ilm. Lie: khashi. Distincte du khawf par la nuance.
words.src: Penrice, A Dictionary and Glossary of the Kor-an, London 1873, s.v. خ ش ي. Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon, London 1863-1893, same root. French sense: Kazimirski, Dictionnaire arabe-francais, Paris 1860, same root. Language fact from those lexicons, not a ruling.

words.en: A close friend, a protector, one placed near. Lane: waliy, one who is near, a friend, a patron, a protector; walayah is nearness and authority to manage. Penrice: A friend, a protector. Allah is wali of the believers. Related: tawalla (he turned to, he took as wali), mawla (master or freed slave, a near one), wilayah. In later speech awliya' Allah are the allies of Allah; the lexicon is nearness and protection, not a rank sold as a title.
words.fr: Un ami proche, un protecteur, un place pres. Lane: waliy, un proche, un ami, un patron; walayah, proximite et autorite de gerer. Penrice: ami, protecteur. Allah est wali des croyants. Lie: tawalla, mawla, wilayah. Dans un langage ulterieur, awliya Allah; le lexique est proximite et protection, non un titre vendu.
words.src: Penrice, A Dictionary and Glossary of the Kor-an, London 1873, s.v. و ل ي. Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon, London 1863-1893, same root. French sense: Kazimirski, Dictionnaire arabe-francais, Paris 1860, same root. Language fact from those lexicons, not a ruling.

words.en: Intercession: joining a plea to another's need. Lane: shafa'a, he interceded; shaf' is a pair (even number), so shafa'ah is adding yourself as a second to someone's case. Penrice: Intercession. Related: shafi' (intercessor), shaf' (even, as opposed to witr, odd). The lexicon is pairing a request, not a right to overrule Allah.
words.fr: Intercession: joindre une supplique au besoin d un autre. Lane: shafa a, il a intercede; shaf, une paire, donc shafa ah, s ajouter comme second a la cause de quelqu un. Penrice: intercession. Lie: shafi, shaf (pair, oppose a witr, impair). Le lexique est d apparier une demande, non un droit de casser le decret d Allah.
words.src: Penrice, A Dictionary and Glossary of the Kor-an, London 1873, s.v. ش ف ع. Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon, London 1863-1893, same root. French sense: Kazimirski, Dictionnaire arabe-francais, Paris 1860, same root. Language fact from those lexicons, not a ruling.

words.en: A throne, a raised seat of rule; the Throne. Lane: arsh, a throne, a roof of palmboughs, a structure raised. Penrice: A throne. Al-Arsh in the Quran is the Throne of Allah, described as being borne and as being above. The lexicon is a throne of kingship, not a chair of a body. Related: arasha (he constructed a trellis).
words.fr: Un trone, un siege eleve de commandement; le Trone. Lane: arsh, un trone, un toit de palmes, une structure elevee. Penrice: un trone. Al-Arsh dans le Coran est le Trone d Allah. Le lexique est un trone de royaute, non une chaise d un corps. Lie: arasha (construire une treille).
words.src: Penrice, A Dictionary and Glossary of the Kor-an, London 1873, s.v. ع ر ش. Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon, London 1863-1893, same root. French sense: Kazimirski, Dictionnaire arabe-francais, Paris 1860, same root. Language fact from those lexicons, not a ruling.

words.en: A seat, a footstool, a chair of knowledge or of rule. Lane: kursiyy, a seat, a chair. Penrice: A throne, a chair. The ayah of the Kursi (2:255) uses this word. Some lexica distinguish kursiyy (seat) from arsh (throne) as lesser to greater; that is a lexical shade, not a diagram of unseen furniture.
words.fr: Un siege, un marchepied, une chaise de savoir ou de commandement. Lane: kursiyy, un siege. Penrice: trone, chaise. Le verset du Kursi (2:255) use ce mot. Certains lexiques distinguent kursiyy et arsh comme moindre et plus grand: une nuance lexicale, non un dessin de meubles invisibles.
words.src: Penrice, A Dictionary and Glossary of the Kor-an, London 1873, s.v. ك ر س. Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon, London 1863-1893, same root. French sense: Kazimirski, Dictionnaire arabe-francais, Paris 1860, same root. Language fact from those lexicons, not a ruling.

words.en: That which is absent from the senses, the unseen. Lane: ghayb, absence, the unseen; ghaba, he was absent. Penrice: The unseen. Related: gha'ib (absent), ghaybah (absence), mughayyab. Opposite of shahadah in the pair al-ghayb wa ash-shahadah: the unseen and the witnessed. Knowledge of the ghayb in the Quran is Allah's; the lexicon is simply what is not present to you.
words.fr: Ce qui est absent des sens, l invisible. Lane: ghayb, absence, l invisible; ghaba, il a ete absent. Penrice: l invisible. Lie: gha ib, ghaybah. Oppose de shahadah dans la paire al-ghayb wa ash-shahadah. La connaissance du ghayb dans le Coran est a Allah; le lexique est ce qui ne t est pas present.
words.src: Penrice, A Dictionary and Glossary of the Kor-an, London 1873, s.v. غ ي ب. Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon, London 1863-1893, same root. French sense: Kazimirski, Dictionnaire arabe-francais, Paris 1860, same root. Language fact from those lexicons, not a ruling.

words.en: A watering-place, a path to water, then a revealed law as a path. Lane: shari'ah, a way to water, a law of religion. Penrice: A law. Related: shara'a (he ordained a path), mashra'ah, shar'. The image is a clear way down to water that cattle can enter: a deen made walkable, not a maze.
words.fr: Un abreuvoir, un chemin vers l eau, puis une loi revelee comme voie. Lane: shari ah, un chemin vers l eau, une loi de religion. Penrice: une loi. Lie: shara a, shar. L image est une voie claire vers l eau ou le betail peut entrer: une religion praticable, non un labyrinthe.
words.src: Penrice, A Dictionary and Glossary of the Kor-an, London 1873, s.v. ش ر ع. Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon, London 1863-1893, same root. French sense: Kazimirski, Dictionnaire arabe-francais, Paris 1860, same root. Language fact from those lexicons, not a ruling.

words.en: A religion, a way of a community, especially the millah of Ibrahim. Lane: millah, a religion, a way. Penrice: A religion. Related in speech to ummah, but millah is the rite-and-creed way, ummah the people on it. Ibrahim's millah is named in the Quran as hanif, inclining away from shirk.
words.fr: Une religion, une voie d une communaute, surtout la millah d Ibrahim. Lane: millah, une religion, une voie. Penrice: une religion. Voisin d ummah, mais millah est la voie de rite et de credo, ummah le peuple qui s y tient. La millah d Ibrahim est dite hanif dans le Coran.
words.src: Penrice, A Dictionary and Glossary of the Kor-an, London 1873, s.v. م ل ل. Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon, London 1863-1893, same root. French sense: Kazimirski, Dictionnaire arabe-francais, Paris 1860, same root. Language fact from those lexicons, not a ruling.

words.en: One who inclines away from error toward the straight; used of Ibrahim. Lane: hanif, one who inclines from a crooked religion to the true; hanaf is an inclination of the foot. Penrice: A true believer, orthodox. Plural hunafa'. The lexicon is an incline toward tawhid, away from the millah of shirk.
words.fr: Celui qui s ecarte de l erreur vers le droit; dit d Ibrahim. Lane: hanif, celui qui penche d une religion courbe vers la vraie; hanaf, inclination du pied. Penrice: vrai croyant. Pluriel hunafa. Le lexique est un penchant vers le tawhid, loin de la millah du shirk.
words.src: Penrice, A Dictionary and Glossary of the Kor-an, London 1873, s.v. ح ن ف. Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon, London 1863-1893, same root. French sense: Kazimirski, Dictionnaire arabe-francais, Paris 1860, same root. Language fact from those lexicons, not a ruling.

words.en: Makkah, the town of the Sacred House. Penrice: Mecca. Lane lists Makkah as the well-known city. Bakkah is used in the Quran as another name of the site (3:96). The lexicon treats them as names of the place, not as metaphors.
words.fr: Makkah, la ville de la Maison sacree. Penrice: La Mecque. Lane liste Makkah comme la ville connue. Bakkah est un autre nom du lieu dans le Coran (3:96). Le lexique les tient pour des noms de lieu.
words.src: Penrice, A Dictionary and Glossary of the Kor-an, London 1873, s.v. م ك ك. Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon, London 1863-1893, same root. French sense: Kazimirski, Dictionnaire arabe-francais, Paris 1860, same root. Language fact from those lexicons, not a ruling.

words.en: A city; al-Madinah, the City of the Prophet, formerly Yathrib. Lane: madinah, a city; plural mudun. Penrice: A city. Related: madani (of the city), tamaddun (later word for civilisation, built on city). Without the article, any town; with the article in Islamic speech, that city.
words.fr: Une ville; al-Madinah, la Ville du Prophete, autrefois Yathrib. Lane: madinah, une ville; pluriel mudun. Penrice: une ville. Sans article, toute ville; avec l article dans la langue islamique, cette ville-la.
words.src: Penrice, A Dictionary and Glossary of the Kor-an, London 1873, s.v. م د ن. Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon, London 1863-1893, same root. French sense: Kazimirski, Dictionnaire arabe-francais, Paris 1860, same root. Language fact from those lexicons, not a ruling.

words.en: Dawn, the splitting of the dark by the first light. Lane: fajr, daybreak; fajara, he split, he caused to gush. Penrice: Daybreak. Salah al-Fajr is the prayer of that time. Related: tafjir (causing springs to burst), fujur (immorality, a "splitting" from what is right, another use of the root).
words.fr: L aube, la fente de la nuit par la premiere lumiere. Lane: fajr, poindre du jour; fajara, il a fendu, il a fait jaillir. Penrice: poindre du jour. La salat al-Fajr est la priere de ce temps. Lie: tafjir, fujur (immoralite, autre emploi de la racine).
words.src: Penrice, A Dictionary and Glossary of the Kor-an, London 1873, s.v. ف ج ر. Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon, London 1863-1893, same root. French sense: Kazimirski, Dictionnaire arabe-francais, Paris 1860, same root. Language fact from those lexicons, not a ruling.

words.en: Noon, the back of the day when the sun is high; zuhr prayer. Lane: zuhr, midday; zahr, the back. Penrice: Midday. Related: zahara (it appeared, it became outward), zahir (outward), zahirah (the heat of noon). Dhuhr salah begins after the sun has passed the zenith, a fiqh timing on this lexical noon.
words.fr: Midi, le dos du jour quand le soleil est haut; la priere du zuhr. Lane: zuhr, midi; zahr, le dos. Penrice: midi. Lie: zahara, zahir, zahirah (chaleur de midi). La salat du Dhuhr commence apres le zenith: un horaire de fiqh sur ce midi lexical.
words.src: Penrice, A Dictionary and Glossary of the Kor-an, London 1873, s.v. ظ ه ر. Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon, London 1863-1893, same root. French sense: Kazimirski, Dictionnaire arabe-francais, Paris 1860, same root. Language fact from those lexicons, not a ruling.

words.en: Late afternoon, an age, a pressing. Lane: asr, afternoon; asr, an epoch; asara, he pressed (juice). Penrice: Time, the afternoon. Surah al-Asr swears by this. Salah al-Asr is the prayer of the declining day. Related: asir (captive, one "pressed"), i'sar.
words.fr: Fin d apres-midi, une epoque, un pressage. Lane: asr, apres-midi; asr, une epoque; asara, il a presse. Penrice: le temps, l apres-midi. La sourate al-Asr jure par cela. La salat al-Asr est la priere du jour qui decline. Lie: asir (captif).
words.src: Penrice, A Dictionary and Glossary of the Kor-an, London 1873, s.v. ع ص ر. Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon, London 1863-1893, same root. French sense: Kazimirski, Dictionnaire arabe-francais, Paris 1860, same root. Language fact from those lexicons, not a ruling.

words.en: The place or time of sunset, the west. Lane: maghrib, sunset, the west; gharaba, the sun set, it went away. Penrice: The west, sunset. Salah al-Maghrib is the prayer at that disappearance of the sun. Related: ghurub (setting), gharib (a stranger, one far from home, another shade of the root "going far").
words.fr: Le lieu ou le temps du coucher du soleil, l ouest. Lane: maghrib, coucher, l ouest; gharaba, le soleil s est couche. Penrice: l ouest, le coucher. La salat al-Maghrib est la priere a cette disparition. Lie: ghurub, gharib (etranger, autre ombre de la racine).
words.src: Penrice, A Dictionary and Glossary of the Kor-an, London 1873, s.v. غ ر ب. Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon, London 1863-1893, same root. French sense: Kazimirski, Dictionnaire arabe-francais, Paris 1860, same root. Language fact from those lexicons, not a ruling.

words.en: The first part of the night, the evening meal time; isha prayer. Lane: isha', the beginning of darkness after Maghrib, the evening. Penrice: The evening. Related: asha (he ate the evening meal), ashiyyah (evening). Salah al-Isha is the prayer of that nightfall.
words.fr: Le debut de la nuit, l heure du repas du soir; la priere de l isha. Lane: isha, le debut de l obscurite apres le Maghrib. Penrice: le soir. Lie: asha (manger le repas du soir), ashiyyah. La salat al-Isha est la priere de cette tombee de la nuit.
words.src: Penrice, A Dictionary and Glossary of the Kor-an, London 1873, s.v. ع ش و. Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon, London 1863-1893, same root. French sense: Kazimirski, Dictionnaire arabe-francais, Paris 1860, same root. Language fact from those lexicons, not a ruling.

words.en: The last part of the night before dawn. Lane: sahar, the time before daybreak. Penrice: The dawn, the time just before it. Related: sahur (the pre-dawn meal of the fasting person), sahir. Distinct from sihr (sorcery), which is a different vowelling of a related spelling: sihr is covering the truth with a trick; sahar is the thinning dark.
words.fr: La fin de la nuit avant l aube. Lane: sahar, le temps avant le poindre. Penrice: l aube, le temps juste avant. Lie: sahur (repas d avant l aube du jeuneur). Distinct de sihr (sorcellerie), autre voyelle: le sihr recouvre la verite d un artifice; le sahar est le noir qui s amincit.
words.src: Penrice, A Dictionary and Glossary of the Kor-an, London 1873, s.v. س ح ر. Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon, London 1863-1893, same root. French sense: Kazimirski, Dictionnaire arabe-francais, Paris 1860, same root. Language fact from those lexicons, not a ruling.

words.en: Holding back, withholding; the stop of eating at Fajr. Lane: amsaka, he held, he withheld; imsak is holding. Penrice: To hold, to withhold. Related: mask (holding), mismak. In fasting speech, imsak is the moment one holds back from food. The same root gives miskin in a different pattern (one who has little to hold).
words.fr: Retenir, retenir; l arret de manger au Fajr. Lane: amsaka, il a retenu; imsak, retenue. Penrice: tenir, retenir. Dans le langage du jeune, l imsak est l instant ou l on se retient de la nourriture.
words.src: Penrice, A Dictionary and Glossary of the Kor-an, London 1873, s.v. م س ك. Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon, London 1863-1893, same root. French sense: Kazimirski, Dictionnaire arabe-francais, Paris 1860, same root. Language fact from those lexicons, not a ruling.

words.en: Breaking the fast; opening the fast at Maghrib. Lane: aftara, he broke his fast; iftar is that breaking. Penrice: To breakfast, to break a fast. See fitrah. Related: fatur, muftir (one who is not fasting). The lexical image is splitting the sawm open.
words.fr: Rompre le jeune; l ouvrir au Maghrib. Lane: aftara, il a rompu son jeune; iftar, cette rupture. Penrice: dejeuner, rompre un jeune. Voir fitrah. Lie: muftir. L image lexicale est de fendre le sawm.
words.src: Penrice, A Dictionary and Glossary of the Kor-an, London 1873, s.v. ف ط ر. Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon, London 1863-1893, same root. French sense: Kazimirski, Dictionnaire arabe-francais, Paris 1860, same root. Language fact from those lexicons, not a ruling.

words.en: Odd number; the witr prayer of odd rakahs at night. Lane: witr, odd (as opposed to shaf', even); also a wrong that leaves one "odd" by taking a kin. Penrice: Odd number. Related: watara, tawatur. The salah called witr is named from being an odd unit after the even pairs of night prayer.
words.fr: Nombre impair; la priere du witr, rakahs impaires de la nuit. Lane: witr, impair (oppose a shaf, pair). Penrice: nombre impair. La salat dite witr est nommee d etre une unite impaire apres les paires de la nuit.
words.src: Penrice, A Dictionary and Glossary of the Kor-an, London 1873, s.v. و ت ر. Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon, London 1863-1893, same root. French sense: Kazimirski, Dictionnaire arabe-francais, Paris 1860, same root. Language fact from those lexicons, not a ruling.

words.en: Friday; the day of gathering. Lane: jumu'ah, Friday, from jama'a, he gathered. Penrice: Friday. Related: jama'ah (a group, a congregation), jam' (gathering), masjid jami' (a congregational mosque), ijma' (agreement, a gathering of views). Salah al-Jumu'ah is the Friday prayer of the gathering.
words.fr: Le vendredi; le jour du rassemblement. Lane: jumu ah, vendredi, de jama a, il a rassemble. Penrice: vendredi. Lie: jama ah, jam, ijma. La salat al-Jumu ah est la priere du rassemblement.
words.src: Penrice, A Dictionary and Glossary of the Kor-an, London 1873, s.v. ج م ع. Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon, London 1863-1893, same root. French sense: Kazimirski, Dictionnaire arabe-francais, Paris 1860, same root. Language fact from those lexicons, not a ruling.

words.en: A returning feast, a festival. Lane: id, a feast, from ada, it returned (a day that returns). Penrice: A festival. Related: awda (he returned), ma'ad (a place of return, the hereafter as return), istia'dah. Id al-Fitr and Id al-Adha are the two named returns of joy in the year.
words.fr: Une fete qui revient, un festival. Lane: id, une fete, de ada, cela est revenu (un jour qui revient). Penrice: une fete. Lie: awda, ma ad (lieu de retour). Id al-Fitr et Id al-Adha sont les deux retours nommes de joie dans l annee.
words.src: Penrice, A Dictionary and Glossary of the Kor-an, London 1873, s.v. ع و د. Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon, London 1863-1893, same root. French sense: Kazimirski, Dictionnaire arabe-francais, Paris 1860, same root. Language fact from those lexicons, not a ruling.

words.en: A path, a road; the straight path, and the Path of the hereafter. Lane: sirat, a way. Penrice: A way, a path. As-sirat al-mustaqim in the Fatiha is the straight road. In hadith speech of the last day, as-sirat is the path over the Fire; the lexicon of Penrice is the Quranic road. Related in sense: tariq, sabil (other words for way).
words.fr: Un chemin, une route; le droit chemin, et le Pont de l au-dela. Lane: sirat, une voie. Penrice: une voie, un chemin. As-sirat al-mustaqim dans la Fatiha. Dans le langage du hadith du dernier jour, as-sirat est la voie sur le Feu; le lexique de Penrice est la route coranique.
words.src: Penrice, A Dictionary and Glossary of the Kor-an, London 1873, s.v. ص ر ط. Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon, London 1863-1893, same root. French sense: Kazimirski, Dictionnaire arabe-francais, Paris 1860, same root. Language fact from those lexicons, not a ruling.

words.en: A balance, scales, a just measure. Lane: mizan, a balance; wazn, weight. Penrice: A balance. Related: wazana (he weighed), mawzun (well-weighed). The mizan of the last day is the scale of deeds in Quranic speech. In this world the word is any just weighing.
words.fr: Une balance, des plateaux, une juste mesure. Lane: mizan, une balance; wazn, poids. Penrice: une balance. Lie: wazana, mawzun. Le mizan du dernier jour est la balance des actes dans la parole coranique. Ici-bas, toute pesee juste.
words.src: Penrice, A Dictionary and Glossary of the Kor-an, London 1873, s.v. و ز ن. Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon, London 1863-1893, same root. French sense: Kazimirski, Dictionnaire arabe-francais, Paris 1860, same root. Language fact from those lexicons, not a ruling.

words.en: Reckoning, account. Lane: hasaba, he reckoned; hisab is an account. Penrice: An account, a reckoning. Yawm al-hisab, the Day of Reckoning. Related: hasib (a reckoner, a name of Allah), ihtisab (taking into account, expecting reward), hasb (sufficiency: hasbunallah).
words.fr: Compte, reglement. Lane: hasaba, il a compte; hisab, un compte. Penrice: un compte, un calcul. Yawm al-hisab. Lie: hasib, ihtisab, hasb (suffisance: hasbunallah).
words.src: Penrice, A Dictionary and Glossary of the Kor-an, London 1873, s.v. ح س ب. Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon, London 1863-1893, same root. French sense: Kazimirski, Dictionnaire arabe-francais, Paris 1860, same root. Language fact from those lexicons, not a ruling.

words.en: A barrier between two things; the interval between death and resurrection. Lane: barzakh, a bar, an interval, a thing between two things. Penrice: A bar, a partition. Quran 55:20, a barzakh between two seas that they do not overpass. In later speech the barzakh is the life of the grave as that interval; the Quranic lexicon is the barrier-interval itself.
words.fr: Une barriere entre deux choses; l intervalle entre la mort et la resurrection. Lane: barzakh, une barre, un intervalle. Penrice: une barre, une cloison. Coran 55:20, un barzakh entre deux mers. Dans un langage ulterieur, le barzakh est la vie de la tombe comme cet intervalle; le lexique coranique est l intervalle-barriere lui-meme.
words.src: Penrice, A Dictionary and Glossary of the Kor-an, London 1873, s.v. ب ر ز خ. Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon, London 1863-1893, same root. French sense: Kazimirski, Dictionnaire arabe-francais, Paris 1860, same root. Language fact from those lexicons, not a ruling.

words.en: A grave. Lane: qabr, a grave; qabara, he buried. Penrice: A grave. Plural qubur. Related: maqbarah (a burial ground). The questioning of the grave is hadith speech; the lexicon is the pit in which the dead are placed.
words.fr: Une tombe. Lane: qabr, une tombe; qabara, il a enterre. Penrice: une tombe. Pluriel qubur. Lie: maqbarah. L interrogation de la tombe est un langage de hadith; le lexique est la fosse ou l on place le mort.
words.src: Penrice, A Dictionary and Glossary of the Kor-an, London 1873, s.v. ق ب ر. Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon, London 1863-1893, same root. French sense: Kazimirski, Dictionnaire arabe-francais, Paris 1860, same root. Language fact from those lexicons, not a ruling.

words.en: Death, the leaving of life. Lane: mawt, death; mata, he died. Penrice: Death. Related: mayyit (dead), mawtah (a death), amat (He caused to die). Opposite: hayah. The Quran uses mawt for the death of the body and, in some ayahs, for a death of the heart; the lexicon starts at the end of hayah.
words.fr: La mort, le quitter de la vie. Lane: mawt, mort; mata, il est mort. Penrice: mort. Lie: mayyit, amat. Oppose: hayah. Le Coran use mawt pour la mort du corps et, en certains versets, pour une mort du coeur; le lexique part de la fin de hayah.
words.src: Penrice, A Dictionary and Glossary of the Kor-an, London 1873, s.v. م و ت. Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon, London 1863-1893, same root. French sense: Kazimirski, Dictionnaire arabe-francais, Paris 1860, same root. Language fact from those lexicons, not a ruling.

words.en: Life. Lane: hayah, life; hayya, he lived. Penrice: Life. Allah is al-Hayy. Related: hayy (living), yuhyi (He gives life), hayawan (in Quranic speech, the true life of the hereafter, 29:64). Al-hayat ad-dunya is this nearer life.
words.fr: La vie. Lane: hayah, vie; hayya, il a vecu. Penrice: vie. Allah est al-Hayy. Lie: hayy, yuhyi, hayawan (dans le Coran, la vraie vie de l au-dela, 29:64). Al-hayat ad-dunya est cette vie plus proche.
words.src: Penrice, A Dictionary and Glossary of the Kor-an, London 1873, s.v. ح ي ي. Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon, London 1863-1893, same root. French sense: Kazimirski, Dictionnaire arabe-francais, Paris 1860, same root. Language fact from those lexicons, not a ruling.

words.en: A devil, a rebellious distant one. Lane: shaytan, a devil; often derived from shatana, he was far, he became rebellious, or from shata, he burned. Penrice: Satan, a devil. Plural shayatin. Iblis is a proper name of the one who refused; shaytan is also used of that one and of every rebellious tempter, jinn or man, in Quranic speech.
words.fr: Un diable, un rebelle eloigne. Lane: shaytan, un diable; souvent de shatana, il s est eloigne, il s est rebelle, ou de shata, il a brule. Penrice: Satan, un diable. Pluriel shayatin. Iblis est un nom propre de celui qui a refuse; shaytan se dit aussi de lui et de tout tentateur rebelle, djinn ou homme.
words.src: Penrice, A Dictionary and Glossary of the Kor-an, London 1873, s.v. ش ط ن. Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon, London 1863-1893, same root. French sense: Kazimirski, Dictionnaire arabe-francais, Paris 1860, same root. Language fact from those lexicons, not a ruling.

words.en: Iblis, the one who despaired and refused. Lane and Penrice: Iblis, a proper name. Often tied to ablasa, he despaired, he was struck silent with grief. Penrice: Eblis. He is called shaytan in many ayahs. The lexicon treats Iblis as that named being who refused sujud to Adam, not as a title of every devil.
words.fr: Iblis, celui qui a desespere et refuse. Lane et Penrice: Iblis, nom propre. Souvent lie a ablasa, il a desespere. Penrice: Eblis. Il est dit shaytan en beaucoup de versets. Le lexique tient Iblis pour cet etre nomme qui a refuse le sujud a Adam, non pour un titre de tout diable.
words.src: Penrice, A Dictionary and Glossary of the Kor-an, London 1873, s.v. ب ل س. Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon, London 1863-1893, same root. French sense: Kazimirski, Dictionnaire arabe-francais, Paris 1860, same root. Language fact from those lexicons, not a ruling.

words.en: The jinn: beings hidden from sight. Lane: jinn, from the root of covering (see jannah). Penrice: Genii, jinn. Related: jannah, janin, junun. They are a created kind in the Quran, made of smokeless fire in the Quranic wording, not metaphors for a mood. Singular jinni / jann in some uses.
words.fr: Les djinns: etres caches a la vue. Lane: jinn, de la racine du cacher (voir jannah). Penrice: genies, djinns. Lie: jannah, janin, junun. Ce sont une espece creee dans le Coran, non des metaphores d une humeur.
words.src: Penrice, A Dictionary and Glossary of the Kor-an, London 1873, s.v. ج ن ن. Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon, London 1863-1893, same root. French sense: Kazimirski, Dictionnaire arabe-francais, Paris 1860, same root. Language fact from those lexicons, not a ruling.

words.en: The human being. Lane: insan, man, a human; uns is sociability, the opposite of being wild. Penrice: Man. Related: ins (mankind, as opposed to jinn), anasa (he was sociable, he perceived), uns. The word marks the companionable creature who is seen, against the jinn who are covered.
words.fr: L etre humain. Lane: insan, l homme, un humain; uns, sociabilite, oppose de l etat sauvage. Penrice: homme. Lie: ins (les hommes, opposes aux djinns), anasa, uns. Le mot marque la creature sociable qui se voit, contre le jinn qui est couvert.
words.src: Penrice, A Dictionary and Glossary of the Kor-an, London 1873, s.v. ا ن س. Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon, London 1863-1893, same root. French sense: Kazimirski, Dictionnaire arabe-francais, Paris 1860, same root. Language fact from those lexicons, not a ruling.

words.en: A slave, a servant, a worshipper. Lane: abd, a slave. Penrice: A servant, a slave. Plural ibad, abid. Every human is abd of Allah by creation; ibadah is the work of that slave when it is given willingly. Related: ibadah, abid, ubudiyyah. Abd Allah is a servant of Allah, a praised name.
words.fr: Un esclave, un serviteur, un adorateur. Lane: abd, un esclave. Penrice: serviteur, esclave. Pluriel ibad, abid. Tout humain est abd d Allah par creation; l ibadah est l oeuvre de cet esclave quand elle est donnee. Lie: ibadah, abid. Abd Allah, serviteur d Allah, un nom loue.
words.src: Penrice, A Dictionary and Glossary of the Kor-an, London 1873, s.v. ع ب د. Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon, London 1863-1893, same root. French sense: Kazimirski, Dictionnaire arabe-francais, Paris 1860, same root. Language fact from those lexicons, not a ruling.

words.en: Ameen: O Allah, respond; so be it. Lane: amin, a word said after a du'a, from the root of amn / iman in the sense of asking that it be so and be secure. Penrice lists amin as "so be it." It is said after al-Fatiha. It is not a verse of the Fatiha in the count of the ayahs; it is a response word of the same root as iman.
words.fr: Amin: O Allah, exauce; qu il en soit ainsi. Lane: amin, mot dit apres un du a, de la racine d amn / iman. Penrice: ainsi soit-il. On le dit apres al-Fatiha. Ce n est pas un verset de la Fatiha dans le compte des ayahs; c est un mot de reponse de la meme racine que iman.
words.src: Penrice, A Dictionary and Glossary of the Kor-an, London 1873, s.v. ا م ن. Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon, London 1863-1893, same root. French sense: Kazimirski, Dictionnaire arabe-francais, Paris 1860, same root. Language fact from those lexicons, not a ruling.

words.en: In the name of Allah. Ism is a name, a noun by which a thing is known. Lane: ism, a name; basmalah is the saying of bismillah. Penrice: A name. The full basmalah adds ar-Rahman ar-Rahim. Related: samma (he named), asma' (names), tasmiyah. Beginning an act with the name is seeking barakah by naming the One in whose name you start.
words.fr: Au nom d Allah. Ism, un nom, un nom par lequel on connait une chose. Lane: ism, un nom; basmalah, le dire de bismillah. Penrice: un nom. La basmalah complete ajoute ar-Rahman ar-Rahim. Lie: samma, asma, tasmiyah. Commencer un acte par le nom, c est chercher la barakah en nommant Celui au nom de qui tu commences.
words.src: Penrice, A Dictionary and Glossary of the Kor-an, London 1873, s.v. س م و. Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon, London 1863-1893, same root. French sense: Kazimirski, Dictionnaire arabe-francais, Paris 1860, same root. Language fact from those lexicons, not a ruling.

words.en: Gathering, consensus. Lane: ajma'a, he agreed, he resolved; ijma' is agreement of a group. Penrice: To collect, to agree. In usul al-fiqh, ijma' is the agreement of the mujtahids of an age; that is a technical use on top of the lexical gathering of views. Related: jama'a, jumu'ah, jama'ah.
words.fr: Rassemblement, consensus. Lane: ajma a, il est tombe d accord; ijma, accord d un groupe. Penrice: rassembler, convenir. Dans les usul, l ijma est l accord des mujtahids d une epoque: emploi technique sur le rassemblement lexical. Lie: jama a, jumu ah, jama ah.
words.src: Penrice, A Dictionary and Glossary of the Kor-an, London 1873, s.v. ج م ع. Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon, London 1863-1893, same root. French sense: Kazimirski, Dictionnaire arabe-francais, Paris 1860, same root. Language fact from those lexicons, not a ruling.

words.en: Measuring one thing by another, analogy. Lane: qasa, he measured; qiyas is measurement and analogy. In fiqh, qiyas is joining a new case to a known ruling by a shared cause. The lexicon is the measuring, not a named school. (Lane s.v. q-y-s / q-w-s in the sense of measuring.)
words.fr: Mesurer une chose par une autre, analogie. Lane: qasa, il a mesure; qiyas, mesure et analogie. Dans le fiqh, joindre un cas nouveau a un statut connu par une cause commune. Le lexique est la mesure. (Lane, s.v. mesurer.)
words.src: Penrice, A Dictionary and Glossary of the Kor-an, London 1873, s.v. ق ي س. Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon, London 1863-1893, same root. French sense: Kazimirski, Dictionnaire arabe-francais, Paris 1860, same root. Language fact from those lexicons, not a ruling.

words.en: That which falls due, that which is incumbent. Lane: wajaba, it fell due, it was necessary; wajib is obligatory, a thing that has fallen as a duty. Penrice: To be necessary. In some schools wajib is a grade just under fard; the lexicon itself is simply what is due and binding. Related: wujub, ijab (making due; also the first half of a contract).
words.fr: Ce qui echoue comme du, ce qui s impose. Lane: wajaba, cela est devenu du, necessaire; wajib, obligatoire. Penrice: etre necessaire. Dans certaines ecoles, wajib est un degre sous le fard; le lexique est simplement ce qui est du. Lie: wujub, ijab.
words.src: Penrice, A Dictionary and Glossary of the Kor-an, London 1873, s.v. و ج ب. Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon, London 1863-1893, same root. French sense: Kazimirski, Dictionnaire arabe-francais, Paris 1860, same root. Language fact from those lexicons, not a ruling.

words.en: That which is disliked, hateful to the soul. Lane: kariha, he disliked; makruh is a thing disliked. Penrice: To dislike. In fiqh, makruh is an act rewarded if left, not punished as haram if done, in many schools; that grading is later. The lexicon is simply what is hated or disliked.
words.fr: Ce qui est deteste, odieux a l ame. Lane: kariha, il a deteste; makruh, une chose detestee. Penrice: detester. Dans le fiqh, makruh est un acte recompense si on le laisse, souvent non puni comme haram; ce classement est ulterieur. Le lexique est ce qui est hai ou deteste.
words.src: Penrice, A Dictionary and Glossary of the Kor-an, London 1873, s.v. ك ر ه. Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon, London 1863-1893, same root. French sense: Kazimirski, Dictionnaire arabe-francais, Paris 1860, same root. Language fact from those lexicons, not a ruling.

words.en: That which is made open, permitted, neither commanded nor forbidden. Lane: abaha, he permitted, he made lawful; mubah is permitted. The root baha / b-w-h is connected with making a thing public and open. In fiqh, mubah is the level of the merely allowed. The lexicon is an opened thing, not a recommended thing (that would be mandub / sunnah).
words.fr: Ce qui est rendu ouvert, permis, ni commande ni defendu. Lane: abaha, il a permis; mubah, permis. Dans le fiqh, le niveau du simplement permis. Le lexique est une chose ouverte, non une chose recommandee (ce serait mandub / sunnah).
words.src: Penrice, A Dictionary and Glossary of the Kor-an, London 1873, s.v. ب و ح. Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon, London 1863-1893, same root. French sense: Kazimirski, Dictionnaire arabe-francais, Paris 1860, same root. Language fact from those lexicons, not a ruling.

words.en: A way, a road, a means. Lane: sabil, a way. Penrice: A way. Ibn as-sabil is the traveller, the son of the road. Fi sabil Allah, in the way of Allah, is a Quranic idiom of a path taken for Allah, including fighting, spending, and other acts named in their ayahs. Related: sabila (it flowed, of rain, another shade).
words.fr: Une voie, une route, un moyen. Lane: sabil, une voie. Penrice: une voie. Ibn as-sabil, le voyageur, fils de la route. Fi sabil Allah, dans le sentier d Allah, idiome coranique d un chemin pris pour Allah. Lie: sabila (couler, d une pluie, autre ombre).
words.src: Penrice, A Dictionary and Glossary of the Kor-an, London 1873, s.v. س ب ل. Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon, London 1863-1893, same root. French sense: Kazimirski, Dictionnaire arabe-francais, Paris 1860, same root. Language fact from those lexicons, not a ruling.

words.en: Truthfulness, correspondence of inner and outer. Lane: sidq, truth, sincerity. Penrice: Truth. Related: sadaqa, sadiq, sadiq (friend), siddiq (one who is ever truthful; Abu Bakr as-Siddiq in history, and a Quranic rank). See sadaqah. Opposite: kadhib (lying).
words.fr: Veracite, accord du dedans et du dehors. Lane: sidq, verite, sincerite. Penrice: verite. Lie: sadaqa, sadiq, siddiq. Voir sadaqah. Oppose: kadhib (mensonge).
words.src: Penrice, A Dictionary and Glossary of the Kor-an, London 1873, s.v. ص د ق. Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon, London 1863-1893, same root. French sense: Kazimirski, Dictionnaire arabe-francais, Paris 1860, same root. Language fact from those lexicons, not a ruling.

words.en: Lying, a false report. Lane: kadhaba, he lied; kadhib is falsehood. Penrice: To lie. Related: kadhdhab (a great liar), mukadhdhib (one who cries lies to a messenger). Opposite of sidq. Takdhib is calling a truth a lie.
words.fr: Mensonge, un faux recit. Lane: kadhaba, il a menti; kadhib, faussete. Penrice: mentir. Lie: kadhdhab, mukadhdhib. Oppose du sidq. Takdhib, traiter une verite de mensonge.
words.src: Penrice, A Dictionary and Glossary of the Kor-an, London 1873, s.v. ك ذ ب. Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon, London 1863-1893, same root. French sense: Kazimirski, Dictionnaire arabe-francais, Paris 1860, same root. Language fact from those lexicons, not a ruling.

words.en: A day, from sunrise to sunset, and a period called a day. Lane: yawm, a day. Penrice: A day. Plural ayyam. Yawm ad-din, the Day of Judgment. Related: yawma'idhin (that day). Al-yawm can mean today.
words.fr: Un jour, du lever au coucher, et une periode dite jour. Lane: yawm, un jour. Penrice: un jour. Pluriel ayyam. Yawm ad-din, le Jour du jugement. Al-yawm peut dire aujourd hui.
words.src: Penrice, A Dictionary and Glossary of the Kor-an, London 1873, s.v. ي و م. Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon, London 1863-1893, same root. French sense: Kazimirski, Dictionnaire arabe-francais, Paris 1860, same root. Language fact from those lexicons, not a ruling.

words.en: Night. Lane: layl, night. Penrice: Night. Opposite: nahar (daytime). Related: laylah (a night), layali. Quranic oaths by the night and its covering. Qiyam al-layl is standing in salah in the night.
words.fr: La nuit. Lane: layl, nuit. Penrice: nuit. Oppose: nahar (le jour). Lie: laylah, layali. Serments coraniques par la nuit. Qiyam al-layl, se tenir en salat dans la nuit.
words.src: Penrice, A Dictionary and Glossary of the Kor-an, London 1873, s.v. ل ي ل. Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon, London 1863-1893, same root. French sense: Kazimirski, Dictionnaire arabe-francais, Paris 1860, same root. Language fact from those lexicons, not a ruling.

words.en: Daytime, the period of light. Lane: nahar, day as opposed to layl; nahr is a river (another root pattern: flowing). Penrice: Day. Related: nahar as the bright stretch in which people spread to seek fadl (bounty).
words.fr: Le jour, la periode de lumiere. Lane: nahar, le jour oppose a layl; nahr, une riviere (autre schema: couler). Penrice: jour. Le nahar est l etendue claire ou les gens se dispersent pour chercher un fadl.
words.src: Penrice, A Dictionary and Glossary of the Kor-an, London 1873, s.v. ن ه ر. Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon, London 1863-1893, same root. French sense: Kazimirski, Dictionnaire arabe-francais, Paris 1860, same root. Language fact from those lexicons, not a ruling.

words.en: The sky, heaven, that which is high. Lane: sama', sky, heaven; from a root of height (sama, it was high). Penrice: Heaven, the sky. Plural samawat. Related: ism (name) is sometimes tied by folk etymology to height; Lane treats ism under its own entry. As-samawat wa al-ard, the heavens and the earth.
words.fr: Le ciel, le firmament, ce qui est haut. Lane: sama, ciel; d une racine de hauteur. Penrice: ciel. Pluriel samawat. As-samawat wa al-ard, les cieux et la terre.

words.en: The earth, land, ground. Lane: ard, earth, land. Penrice: The earth. Related: ardi (earthly). Opposite pair with sama'. Fiqh uses ard for the ground of tayammum: clean earth.
words.fr: La terre, le sol, le pays. Lane: ard, terre, pays. Penrice: la terre. Pair oppose a sama. Le fiqh use ard pour le sol du tayammum: terre propre.

words.en: Water. Lane: ma', water. Penrice: Water. The Quran makes every living thing from water. Related: mah (water in some dialects), ma'ih. Tahur is a description of water that purifies, from t-h-r, not from this root.
words.fr: L eau. Lane: ma, eau. Penrice: eau. Le Coran fait toute chose vivante d eau. Tahur est une description de l eau qui purifie, de t-h-r, non de cette racine.

words.en: Fire. Lane: nar, fire; nur is light. Penrice: Fire. An-Nar with the article in religious speech is Hell. Related: nur (light), munir. The two words share a root in the lexica of light and heat, with nar as the burning and nur as the shining.
words.fr: Le feu. Lane: nar, feu; nur, lumiere. Penrice: feu. An-Nar avec l article, dans la langue religieuse, est l Enfer. Lie: nur, munir. Les deux mots partagent une racine de lumiere et de chaleur: nar, le bruler; nur, le luire.

words.en: Great, mighty, vast in rank. Lane: azim, great; azm is a bone (the root covers greatness and bones as the strong frame). Penrice: Great. Allah is al-Azim. Related: azama (it was great), ta'zim (magnifying), izam (bones). A reflection that "greatness is like bone" is not a lexicon ruling; Lane lists both senses of the root without that sermon. See PROJECT on this root.
words.fr: Grand, puissant, vaste en rang. Lane: azim, grand; azm, un os (la racine couvre la grandeur et les os comme charpente). Penrice: grand. Allah est al-Azim. Lie: azama, ta zim, izam. Une reflexion « la grandeur est comme l os » n est pas un jugement du lexique; Lane liste les deux sens sans ce sermon.
